x: There was one unpleasant and entirely unnecessary happening in the Kinnaird Trophy Competition. We refer to the action of some of the officials in not allowing J. Parker to run for us in the 3 miles event.

The 1 Mile came next, and this is always considered by most people to be the tit-bit of the meeting. J. Parker, our new member from Brighton, was an entrant, and right from the start his huge stride took him into the lead.
Carter ran one of his best races to date. Unlike the 1 Mile Championship, he wisely let J. Parker go and worked up to his man gradually.
1937 · Stratford-on-Avon · 2nd · 94 · J. Ginty (1) J. Parker (2) D. Patience (11) H. E. Footer (13) L. J. Cohen (26) C. T. Carter (41)
From the very start Pat Parker looked the winner and after the first mile he was leading, but followed very closely by Carter, Cohen, Stimpson and Ring, with the rest of the field in hot pursuit.
Second Relay (5 2/10 miles).—1, Belgrave H. (J. Parker) 55m. 39s.; 2, Birchfield H. 55m. 48s.; 3, M.A.C. 55m. 59s.

A further invitation having been given by the Union Sportive Metropolitaine for us to compete in the above event was accepted and the following team was chosen to represent the Club---Carter, Cohen, Footer, D. Patience, J. Parker, Penny, Tobin and Verney, accompanied by W.G.
